skill.name: content-strategy
skill.description: Plan content pillars, topic clusters, buyer-stage keywords, and publishing priorities using business goals, customer research, and available resources.
skill.summary: Turn customer insights into prioritized content plans with topic clusters and distribution guidance.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.value_statement: Unstructured content ideas make it difficult to choose topics that support business goals. This skill organizes customer insights into content pillars, ranked topics, and distribution plans.
actual_capabilities: Define three to five content pillars with related topic clusters and product connections.
Map keywords and content formats to awareness, consideration, decision, and implementation stages.
Extract content ideas from supplied keyword exports, customer transcripts, surveys, and sales or support input.
Rank topics using weighted customer impact, product relevance, search potential, and resource scores.
Recommend a starting calendar mix of 60% searchable, 30% shareable, and 10% experimental content.
Plan content repurposing and distribution, with reference guidance for CMS selection, content models, and editorial workflows.
limitations: Live forum and competitor research requires web search access from the host assistant.
Keyword volumes, competition metrics, and customer evidence require supplied data or external research; the skill includes no data connector.
Provides strategy guidance rather than automated publishing, CMS deployment, or analytics tracking.
Refers individual copywriting, technical SEO audits, and detailed social execution to separate skills.

use_cases.title: Launch a focused company blog
use_cases.description: Choose content pillars and initial topics that connect customer problems to a new product and its buying journey.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a content backlog
use_cases.description: Rank proposed articles against customer impact, product relevance, search opportunity, and production capacity.

use_cases.title: Plan reusable content delivery
use_cases.description: Connect topic plans with channel repurposing, reusable CMS content types, and editorial approval stages.

prompt_templates.title: Choose initial content pillars
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan three content pillars for [product] serving [audience]. Our goal is [goal]. Ask for missing context and suggest beginner topics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start a strategy with basic business context.

prompt_templates.title: Build a buyer-stage topic cluster
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a topic cluster for [pillar]. Map each article to a buyer stage, target query, format, and internal linking relationship.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn one pillar into a connected article plan.

prompt_templates.title: Rank ideas using customer evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use these anonymized customer notes and keyword exports to rank [ideas]. Apply the four weighted factors, cite supporting evidence, and label missing data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prioritize a backlog using supplied research.

prompt_templates.title: Create an integrated quarterly plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a quarterly strategy for [product] using [research] and [capacity]. Include ranked topics, buyer stages, calendar allocation, distribution actions, and CMS workflow needs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine production planning, distribution, and editorial operations.

output_examples.input: Plan content for expense management software serving finance teams, with a goal of generating qualified leads.
output: Pillar: expense policy management. Connect practical policy guidance to the product's approval and compliance capabilities.
Awareness topic: How to create an employee expense policy. Format: guide. Proposed target query: employee expense policy.
Consideration topic: Expense management software comparison. Format: comparison. Proposed target query: best expense management software.
Implementation topic: Expense approval workflow template. Format: template. Connect it to the policy guide through internal links.
Validate customer demand and keyword metrics before assigning final priorities.

output_examples.input: Plan distribution for one detailed guide about remote team onboarding.
output: Publish the guide on the company blog and identify sections that work as standalone posts.
Repurpose the guide into four social posts, one carousel, two quote graphics, and one email.
Use social and partner channels for discovery, then direct readers to the guide and an optional email subscription.
Collect audience questions to inform the next onboarding article.

best_practices: Provide business goals, audience details, production capacity, and anonymized customer research before requesting priorities.
Require a distinct contribution for each searchable topic, supported by examples, evidence, or original insights.
Validate keyword assumptions and adjust the proposed calendar mix to team capacity and observed results.
anti_patterns: Treating estimated keyword metrics or unsupported customer assumptions as verified facts.
Publishing unrelated topics without clear links to audience needs, product relevance, or buyer stages.
Creating articles without a distribution plan or relying entirely on social platforms.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide your product, target audience, content goal, existing content, and available resources. Customer questions and keyword exports improve the recommendations.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete blog posts?
faq.answer: Its primary role is planning topics and priorities. It refers full content drafting to a separate copywriting skill.

faq.question: Does it include live keyword metrics?
faq.answer: No. It can analyze supplied exports, but it includes no keyword database or built-in analytics connector.

faq.question: Can it use customer interviews and surveys?
faq.answer: Yes. It extracts recurring questions, objections, themes, and customer language from supplied material. Remove personal and confidential details before sharing.

faq.question: Will it publish content or configure my CMS?
faq.answer: No automated publishing or deployment is included. The references provide CMS selection, content modeling, and editorial workflow guidance.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill provides Markdown instructions for these assistants. Live research depends on the tools available in your environment.
